content:
The image shows a split soybean stem in close-up. Key features:

- **Stem cross-section** split open lengthwise
- **Black sclerotia** (hard, irregularly shaped fungal bodies) visible inside the pith cavity
- **White cottony mycelium** present between the sclerotia and along the interior walls
- **Bleached/straw-colored exterior** of the stem
- Dense white stem hairs (trichomes) visible on the surface

The combination of white cottony mycelium inside a bleached stem along with prominent black sclerotia is the hallmark of **White Mold** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*). The sclerotia are the key diagnostic feature — large, black, irregular bodies formed inside stem cavities. This distinguishes it from Charcoal Rot (which has tiny microsclerotia that look like charcoal dust) or Phomopsis (no sclerotia).
